source.title: Spectrum Dependent Learning Curves in Kernel Regression and Wide Neural Networks
source.authors: Blake Bordelon; Abdulkadir Canatar; Cengiz Pehlevan

record.tranche_reason: The study measures generalization-error learning curves as training sample size changes, using kernel regression and wide neural networks; it does not reproduce a model-capacity double-descent sweep.
record.gate_note: The paper tests sample-size learning curves, including ridgeless kernel regression, and reports total generalization-error results. Its separate spectral-mode error curves (Figures 2–4) are not recorded as total test-error rows. The paper does not sweep model size or training epochs, and it does not report a rise in total error near a located interpolation threshold. Cited findings from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The paper derives and checks average learning curves for noiseless kernel regression and wide networks as sample size grows. It never mentions double descent. It sweeps no model size or epochs and adds no label noise. Its ridgeless kernels have effectively unbounded features, so there is no sample-wise interpolation threshold for V3 to apply to. The Belkin et al. 'Reconciling' paper is cited only in passing, about implicit bias. Its monotone, stage-wise learning curves concern spectral learning order, a different construct from a test-error peak at an interpolation threshold.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors derive an approximate average-case theory of kernel-regression learning curves, decomposed by spectral mode. Kernels and wide networks fit higher spectral modes only as sample size grows, with distinct learning stages on the hypersphere. Total error follows power laws set by the kernel and target spectra, and explicit regularization slows the asymptotic decay. Their theory matches simulations on synthetic data and MNIST. They make no claim about double descent.
record.recipe_differences: Studies sample-size learning curves and spectral learning stages in kernel regression and wide networks; it does not use a model-size double-descent protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning curves depend on the kernel spectrum, input dimension, target spectrum, and regularization parameter; explicit regularization suppresses the reported sharp spectral learning drops.

fits_no_version.finding: In noiseless ridgeless kernel regression and wide networks, error falls with sample size in stages. Modes with larger kernel eigenvalues are learned first, with sharp drops near p≈N(d,k). Explicit regularization smooths these stages and slows the asymptotic power-law decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral-bias learning stages: kernel and wide-network learning curves decrease in stages ordered by kernel eigenvalue, and regularization slows asymptotic decay.

record.problems: The reported total-error curves are mostly figures without numerical values or a textual account of whether error rises anywhere. The theoretical asymptotic scaling does not test behavior locally around an interpolation threshold. Experiments use synthetic tasks and a stated MNIST subset.
record.rows_left_out: Separate mode-wise error curves in Figures 2–4 were left out because they report spectral components rather than total test/generalization error. The paper's training-loss plots in Supplementary Information Figure SI.3 were also left out because training loss is not the test-error measure in the claim.

untested.parts: No test error over training epochs (SI Fig SI.3 shows training loss only).
No sample-wise interpolation threshold, and no label noise; learning curves are not examined for a rise.
No capacity sweep through an interpolation point.
No effective-complexity measure predicting a peak location.
No label noise and no peak. Regularization is varied, but only its effect on asymptotic decay and learning stages is reported.
No re-parameterization of a complexity axis.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and its V3 link are not supported: the study is outside the claim's scope. It has no label noise and no sample-wise interpolation threshold. Later work using the same framework (with noise) addresses sample-wise double descent, but this paper does not.

versions.untested_parts: Model-size sweep and a peak near the size that just fits the training set.
Test error over training epochs or other training time.
The study varies sample size and reports generalization-error curves, but does not isolate or analyze a neighborhood around a double-descent interpolation peak.
Risk as model-class capacity grows through and beyond an interpolation point.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
Whether label noise or variance drives a peak, whether multiple peaks occur, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes a peak.
Whether an effective parameter count transforms a second-descent curve into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: kernel regression
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical sample-size learning-curve scaling for power-law kernel and target spectra.

conditions.value: λ = 0 or low, and explicit λ regimes

rows.measure: Total generalization error Eg; predicted asymptotic scaling with p.
rows.value: Eg ∼ p−min{a−1,2b} for p < λ−1/(b−1); Eg ∼ p−min{a−1,2b}/b for p > λ−1/(b−1).
rows.note: The stated asymptotic scalings decrease with sample size; this is not an analysis of a local interpolation-threshold peak.
rows.check: Asymptotic power-law scaling (SI.43) for p→∞ in noiseless power-law kernel regression. It cannot show a local rise near an interpolation threshold, and this setting has no such threshold. It should not be linked to V3, and 'absent' overstates what it can show.

rows.subject: Gaussian kernel regression
rows.operation_detail: Experimental generalization-error learning curves across sample sizes, with ridge parameter varied.

conditions.value: d = 20 dimensional standard normal random vector data
constructed by the rule in equation 34

rows.measure: Total generalization error Eg versus sample size p.
rows.note: The text says sharp error drops occur around p ≈ N(d,k) for k = 1, 2 when λ is small, and that explicit regularization suppresses these drops; it does not explicitly describe whether total error rises anywhere.
rows.check: Gaussian-kernel learning curves in Fig 4(a). The text describes only sharp drops at p≈N(d,k) that regularization suppresses. No interpolation-threshold axis applies, so the row does not bear on V3.

rows.subject: 2-layer NN student-teacher experiment
rows.operation_detail: Experimental total generalization-error learning curve across sample sizes.
rows.measure: Total generalization error Eg versus sample size p.
rows.uncertainty: standard deviations shown with error bars; numerical values not stated
rows.note: The text says experimental and theoretical curves agree excellently, but does not state the direction of the total-error curve in words.
rows.check: Theory-vs-experiment agreement for a noiseless student-teacher net (Fig 3c). No sample-wise double-descent setting or threshold, so not V3.

rows.subject: 3-layer NN
rows.operation_detail: Experimental total test-error learning curve across sample sizes on MNIST.

conditions.value: subset of 8000 randomly sampled MNIST images

rows.measure: Total test error versus sample size p.
rows.note: The text reports comparison with the NTK learning curve and says the total-generalization-error results agree, but does not state the curve's direction in words.
rows.check: MNIST NN learning curve used to validate the theory (Fig 4b). Reports agreement, not a test of V3.

rows.subject: 3-layer NTK regression
rows.operation_detail: Experimental total test-error learning curve across sample sizes on MNIST.

conditions.value: subset of 8000 randomly sampled MNIST images

rows.measure: Total test error versus sample size p.
rows.note: The text reports agreement with the neural-network experiment and theory, but does not state the direction of the total-error curve in words.
rows.check: MNIST NTK regression curve (Fig 4b, λ=0) used for validation. Not a test of V3. Fig 4(c) actually shows aggregated mode errors, not total error.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The reported asymptotic total-error scalings decline with sample size rather than showing more data raising error; they do not establish behavior near an interpolation peak (r1).
